//: Canonical destructive-command rule table for the cluster repos. This file is the single source of truth: .claude/hooks/guard-destructive.sh and .opencode/plugins/guard-destructive.js are GENERATED from it by gen-guards.py, so the bash and JS guards cannot drift apart. gen-guards.py splits a command into simple commands (quote contents blanked, heredocs and continuations handled, wrappers like sudo/env/xargs and leading VAR=val stripped), then matches each rule's pattern against the start of each one, so a guarded word only counts in command position. Patterns are written in the intersection of Python re and JavaScript RegExp. <<NAME>> expands a macro from 'macros'. A rule has: id, pattern (against the command with quote contents blanked; 'on': 'plain' matches the command with quote marks removed instead), optional exempt (regex on the plain form) or exempt_env (a leading VAR=1 assignment that opts out), optional subagent_only (needs agent_id in the payload; never emitted for opencode), optional decision ('block' by default, or 'ask' for a PreToolUse permissionDecision ask), reason, alternative, optional repos.

always_allow.//: A read-only dry run is never blocked. It applies to one simple command only, so a dry run in one command never excuses the next, and --dry-run=none does not count.

rules.alternative: Apply through the apply-ks task of the cluster: 'mise run //kube/clusters/<cluster>:apply-ks <ns> <ks>'. cordon, uncordon and rollout are not blocked.

rules.exempt_reason: PVC recreation (miroir StorageClass migrations, restore drills) is routine and always paired with a verified kopiur snapshot. The marker opts a single command out of THIS rule only, and only as a leading env assignment (I_HAVE_A_KOPIUR_SNAPSHOT=1 kubectl delete pvc ...); a comment or an echo does not count. Every other rule, including talosctl reset/wipe, still applies. Runbook: .agents/skills/recreate-pvc. Frostlink restores go through 'mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink:restore-pvc' (kopiur-restore skill) and need no marker.
rules.alternative: Confirm with the user before deleting cluster resources. If this is a planned PVC recreation with a verified snapshot, prefix the command with I_HAVE_A_KOPIUR_SNAPSHOT=1 (see .agents/skills/recreate-pvc); on Frostlink use 'mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink:restore-pvc' instead

rules.reason: Direct helm mutations are not allowed — config lives in HelmRelease manifests
rules.alternative: Edit the HelmRelease values and apply via Flux

rules.reason: helmfile sync/apply/destroy/delete changes a live cluster outside GitOps
rules.alternative: Use the bootstrap tasks ('mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink/bootstrap:phase1' and the rebuild order in oci-rebuild.md), with the user watching
Confirm with the user before deleting Flux resources

rules.reason: A bare tofu/terraform write skips the repo's task wrapper, which sets the workspace, credentials and the import-first check
rules.alternative: Use the mise tasks: 'mise run //terraform:plan', and with the user's go-ahead 'mise run --yes //terraform:apply'

rules.reason: talosctl patch machineconfig duplicates array fields (machine.files etc.) and can brick the node
rules.alternative: Artemis: 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis/talos:apply-node <node>' or talosctl apply-config --file for full config replacement. Frostlink: a minimal DELTA patch file, or 'talosctl apply-config --file' — never pass kube/clusters/frostlink/talos/patches/controlplane.yaml, it is a gen-time patch and will strand the node

rules.reason: talosctl reset/wipe is destructive and irreversible
rules.alternative: Confirm explicitly with the user before proceeding

rules.exempt_reason: A bare talosctl call cannot say which cluster it targets, so it is treated as Frostlink unless the command selects Artemis: '--context artemis' or the artemis talosconfig path. The word 'artemis' elsewhere in the command does not count. The mise tasks run talosctl inside the task, so this rule never sees them.
rules.reason: Frostlink is a single node — talosctl upgrade/reboot/shutdown is a FULL cluster outage with nothing to fail over to. This command does not select Artemis, so it may target Frostlink
rules.alternative: Frostlink: 'mise run //kube/clusters/frostlink/talos:upgrade <version>' (it resolves the schematic first), and only with the user watching. Artemis: 'mise run //kube/clusters/artemis/talos:upgrade-node <node>', or select Artemis in the command (--context artemis or its talosconfig path)

rules.reason: Recursive delete on a sensitive path
rules.alternative: Confirm the exact path with the user before deleting. A path below /home/<user>/<dir>, such as a worktree, is not blocked

rules.reason: mv into ~/.claude, ~/.config, ~/.agents or ~/.local/bin REPLACES a mise-managed symlink with a regular file, silently unlinking it from ~/dotfiles — edits then stop reaching the repo
rules.alternative: Use `cp` instead of `mv`, which writes through the symlink and keeps it intact

rules.reason: A subagent is about to run a mise task that writes: it can change a live cluster, a host or the cloud. The safety is the procedure around the task (suspend root and target, watch, wait for confirmation, resume in order), and a subagent skips all of it. The owner has to allow each one.
rules.alternative: Validate offline instead ('mise run //kube/clusters/<cluster>:render-ks <ns> <ks>'), or read live state with diff-ks. If the write is wanted, approve this prompt.

rules.reason: A subagent is about to write to git history or the working tree (stage, commit, push, rebase, merge, reset, checkout, stash, cherry-pick, branch delete). The owner has to allow each one. This is a PreToolUse hook, so it holds under every permission mode.
rules.alternative: Leave the working tree dirty and report what you changed, or approve this prompt. Read-only git (status, log, diff, show, worktree) is unaffected.
